summary: Build practical AAP skills with CHS, IASC guidance, complaints workflows, and feedback tracking. Train your team to close the loop with communities.
lede: Accountability to affected populations gives humanitarian professionals practical methods to connect community concerns with documented action. Participants learn to assess accountability gaps, map stakeholders, and design feedback and complaints workflows with safe referral and communication processes. They also practice analyzing feedback, tracking response timelines, and reporting findings to support changes in humanitarian activities.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for humanitarian professionals who need stronger accountability systems, cleaner feedback workflows, and better reporting on community concerns. It is especially relevant if you work across community engagement, MEAL, protection, safeguarding, programme management, or partner coordination.
prerequisites: You need a laptop capable of running Excel or an equivalent spreadsheet tool, plus the ability to read and draft simple program documents. Bring a basic understanding of humanitarian operations, and if possible, sample feedback forms, complaints logs, or MEAL reporting templates from your work context.
